quiz.title: Indefinite Integration MCQ Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight objective-type questions on indefinite integration covering standard results, substitution, integration by parts and partial fractions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.explanation: The derivative of tan x is sec<sup>2</sup>x, so ∫ sec<sup>2</sup>x dx = tan x + C.
This is a standard result: ∫ dx/(1 + x<sup>2</sup>) = tan<sup>−1</sup>x + C.
Put t = x<sup>2</sup>, so dt = 2x dx. Then ∫ cos t dt = sin t + C = sin(x<sup>2</sup>) + C.
Write tan x = sin x/cos x and put t = cos x. The result is −ln|cos x| + C, i.e. ln|sec x| + C.
Take u = x, dv = e<sup>x</sup>dx. Then ∫ x e<sup>x</sup> dx = x e<sup>x</sup> − ∫ e<sup>x</sup> dx = x e<sup>x</sup> − e<sup>x</sup> + C.

questions.q: ∫ e<sup>x</sup>(sin x + cos x) dx equals
questions.explanation: This is the ∫ e<sup>x</sup>[f(x) + f′(x)] dx form with f(x) = sin x, giving e<sup>x</sup> f(x) + C = e<sup>x</sup> sin x + C.
1/((x−1)(x−2)) = 1/(x−2) − 1/(x−1). Integrating gives ln|x−2| − ln|x−1| + C = ln|(x−2)/(x−1)| + C.
This is the standard inverse-trig result: ∫ dx/√(1 − x<sup>2</sup>) = sin<sup>−1</sup>x + C.

faq.q: What kinds of objective questions come from indefinite integration in Class 12?
faq.a: Most MCQs test recall of standard results, spotting the right substitution, choosing u and dv for integration by parts, and splitting a rational function into partial fractions. Recognising which method a form needs is usually half the battle.

faq.q: How do I decide between substitution and integration by parts?
faq.a: If the integrand contains a function and its derivative (up to a constant), substitution is the natural choice. If it is a product of two unrelated functions such as a polynomial times an exponential or a log, integration by parts (ILATE order) is usually the way.

faq.q: Do I need to add the constant of integration in MCQs?
faq.a: Yes. An indefinite integral is a family of functions, so the correct option always carries + C. Options that omit it or fix a particular value are deliberate distractors.

faq.q: Which standard results are worth memorising for objective questions?
faq.a: Learn the integrals of the six trig functions, the three inverse-trig forms (1/(1 + x²), 1/√(1 − x²) and their partners), 1/x, e^x, a^x, and the e^x[f + f′] pattern. These cover the bulk of single-line MCQs.
